evidence_items.source_quote: screening for syphilis (VDRL), toxoplasmosis antibody, and Cryptococcus antigen titers were negative.

rationale: A 31-year-old male with newly diagnosed HIV/AIDS presenting with progressive dyspnea, weight loss, ophthalmoplegia, ataxia, and altered mental status. Brain MRI demonstrated symmetrical T2 hyperintensity in the periaqueductal gray and medial thalami consistent with Wernicke's encephalopathy. Infectious evaluation for intracranial opportunistic infections, specifically including Cryptococcus antigen titers, was negative. Cryptococcosis was tested and ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Bacteria, fungi, cryptococcus, and Mycobacterium tuberculosis were all negative;

rationale: A 21-year-old male presenting with fever, watery diarrhea, and subsequent symmetric flaccid quadriplegia and hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis triggered by Campylobacter jejuni enteritis. CSF analysis showed normal biochemistry and negative staining and culture for bacteria, fungi, cryptococcus, and tuberculosis. Cryptococcosis was ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Mycobacterium tuberculosis, atypical mycobacteria, cytomegalovirus, Cryptococcus and Aspergillus species, were negative.

rationale: A 24-year-old female with primary immune thrombocytopenia treated with rituximab who developed severe late hypogammaglobulinemia presenting with high fever and septic shock. Infectious workup for opportunistic pathogens including Cryptococcus and Aspergillus was negative. Blood cultures grew Enterococcus faecium. Cryptococcosis was ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Serology and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) tests for HIV, cryptococcus, syphilis, tuberculosis, bacteria, fungus, and virus showed no evidence of inflammation.

rationale: A 36-year-old male presenting with progressive cognitive decline, tremor, and frontotemporal dementia-like syndrome diagnosed with genetic Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease (G114V mutation). Extensive CSF and serological tests for cryptococcus and other infectious etiologies were negative. Cryptococcosis ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Tests for Cryptococcus antigen, Toxoplasmosis antigen, Ebstein Barr virus IgG and IgM, Cytomegalovirus IgG and IgM, Hepes Simplex virus polymerase chain reaction (PCR), Japanese encephalitis as well as cultures for tuberculosis and fungi (plasma and cerebrospinal fluid, CSF) were all negative.

rationale: An 8-year-old HIV-infected male child presenting with progressive right hemiparesis and neurological decline diagnosed with progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (JCV PCR positive). CSF Cryptococcus antigen was negative. Cryptococcosis ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Tests were negative for Pneumocystis jirovecii, acid fast bacilli, cytomegalovirus, parvovirus, Epstein-Barr virus, cryptococcus, histoplasmosis, syphilis, and influenza A.

rationale: A 36-year-old male with acute HIV seroconversion presenting with fever and viral illness. Comprehensive infectious workup including cryptococcus and histoplasmosis was negative. Cryptococcosis ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Meningitis/encephalitis panel (PCR testing for Escherichia coli K1, Haemophilus influenzae, Listeria monocytogenes, Neisseria meningitidis (encapsulated), Streptococcus agalactiae, Streptococcus pneumoniae, Cytomegalovirus, Enterovirus, Herpes Simplex virus 1 and 2, Human Herpesvirus 6, Human Parecho virus, Varicella zoster virus, Cryptococcus neoformans/gattii) was negative.

rationale: A 68-year-old male with metastatic squamous cell lung carcinoma receiving pembrolizumab presenting with altered mental status diagnosed with immune-checkpoint inhibitor autoimmune encephalopathy. CSF meningitis panel including Cryptococcus neoformans/gattii was negative. Cryptococcosis ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Multiplex polymerase chain reaction (PCR) of the CSF was negative for cytomegalovirus (CMV), Cryptococcus neoformans, Escherichia coli, Enterovirus, Haemophilus influenzae B, human herpesvirus 6 (HHV-6), human parechovirus, herpes simplex virus (HSV) 1/2, Listeria monocytogenes, Neisseria meningitidis, Streptococcus agalactiae (group B streptococcus (GBS)), Streptococcus pneumoniae, and varicella zoster virus (VZV).

rationale: A 44-year-old female presenting with profound obtundation, severe hypernatremia, and osmotic extrapontine myelinolysis. CSF PCR panel for CNS pathogens including Cryptococcus neoformans was negative. Cryptococcosis ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Other causes than neoplastic lesion were ruled out, including cryptococcosis, toxoplasmosis, syphilis, or human immunodeficiency virus infection.

rationale: A 56-year-old male presenting with headache and confusion found to have intracranial mass lesions diagnosed as metastatic intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma. Infectious causes including cryptococcosis and toxoplasmosis were formally evaluated and ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: No Mycobacterium or Cryptococcus infections were identified, and serum aquaporin 4 antibody was negative.

rationale: A 70-year-old male with Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia presenting with progressive weakness and cauda equina syndrome diagnosed with relapsed Bing-Neel syndrome. CSF testing was negative for Mycobacterium and Cryptococcus. Cryptococcosis ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: pathogens of toxoplasmosis and cryptococcosis, and Coxiella burnetii, were negative.
evidence_items.test_name: Serological test for pathogens of cryptococcosis

rationale: An 18-year-old pregnant female presented with fever, headache, vomiting, and limb weakness, initially diagnosed with viral meningoencephalitis and subsequently confirmed with acute disseminated encephalomyelitis (ADEM). Serological screening for infectious pathogens, including pathogens of cryptococcosis, was negative. Cryptococcosis was tested and ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: as was serologic testing for Treponema pallidum, Cryptococcus, Histoplasma, Coccidioides, and Brucella.

rationale: A 61-year-old male presented with malaise, cough, weight loss, and a large retroperitoneal mass with lumbar vertebral destruction, ultimately confirmed to be Q fever (Coxiella burnetii) by tissue PCR. Serological testing for Cryptococcus was unrevealing/negative. Cryptococcosis was investigated and ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Negative Fontana-Masson and mucicarmine stains excluded the presence of a Cryptococcus sp.

rationale: A 68-year-old male presented with a recurrent crusted keratotic facial plaque diagnosed as Histoplasma capsulatum infection confirmed by tissue NGS. Special histological stains for Cryptococcus sp. (Fontana-Masson and mucicarmine) were negative, excluding Cryptococcus. Cryptococcosis was tested and ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Tests for other viral (CMV, EBV, VZV, HSV, dengue), fungal (Histoplasma, Cryptococcus), bacterial (Bartonella, Rickettsia, Legionella, Mycobacterium) and parasitic (Leishmania, Toxocara) pathogens were negative.

rationale: A 14-year-old male with WHIM syndrome presenting with acute right eye blindness, diagnosed with active ocular toxoplasmosis confirmed by vitreous PCR for T. gondii. Diagnostic workup for fungal pathogens including Cryptococcus was negative. Cryptococcosis was tested and ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Serological assays showed positive results for IgM antibodies to Parainfluenza virus, but negative results for antibodies to respiratory syncytial virus, influenza virus (types A and B), cytomegalovirus (CMV), Adenovirus, Legionella pneumophila, Mycoplasma pneumonia, Chlamydia pneumoniae, Q-rickettsia, and Cryptococcus neoformans.
evidence_items.test_name: Serological antibody assay for Cryptococcus neoformans

rationale: A 27-year-old female kidney transplant recipient on immunosuppression presenting with cough, fever, and dyspnea, diagnosed with severe Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia confirmed by BALF mNGS. Serological screening for Cryptococcus neoformans antibodies was negative. Cryptococcosis was evaluated and ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Tests for pathogens that included Epstein-Barr virus (EBV), cytomegalovirus (CMV), cryptococcus, tuberculosis, and parasites were negative; blood cultures for bacteria, acid-fast bacilli, and fungi were also negative.
evidence_items.test_name: Pathogen testing for cryptococcus and blood fungal culture

rationale: A 23-year-old male presenting with fever, vomiting, and splenomegaly, ultimately diagnosed with NK/T cell lymphoma by bone marrow biopsy and Onco-mNGS. Extensive pathogen screening including specific testing for cryptococcus and fungal blood cultures was negative. Cryptococcosis was tested and ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: negative xanthochromia, negative bacterial and fungal culture, negative cryptococcus antigen, and negative meningoencephalitis viral panel.
evidence_items.test_name: CSF cryptococcus antigen and fungal culture

rationale: A 32-year-old female presenting with sudden thunderclap headache and lymphocytic pleocytosis, diagnosed with syndrome of transient headache and neurological deficits with cerebrospinal fluid lymphocytosis (HaNDL). CSF cryptococcus antigen and fungal culture were negative. Cryptococcosis was investigated and ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Lumbar puncture was negative for syphilis, toxoplasmosis, Cryptococcus, Cytomegalovirus and Epstein-Barr Virus.
evidence_items.test_name: Lumbar puncture opportunistic infection panel for Cryptococcus

rationale: A 34-year-old male with newly diagnosed advanced HIV infection (CD4 89 cells/microL) presenting with spastic paraparesis and myelopathy. Lumbar puncture was performed to evaluate for opportunistic central nervous system infections, and CSF testing was negative for Cryptococcus. Cryptococcosis was tested and ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: There were no bacteria, Cryptococcus or acid-resistant bacilli in the CSF smear.

rationale: A 61-year-old female presenting with acute ptosis, diplopia, and proximal extremity weakness, diagnosed with generalized myasthenia gravis with positive AChR antibodies and positive neostigmine test. Diagnostic CSF examination showed no Cryptococcus on smear. Cryptococcosis was ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Serologies for aspergillus, blastomycosis, coccidioides, cryptococcus, histoplasma, HIV, and toxoplasma were negative.

rationale: A 72-year-old male with chronic lymphocytic leukemia presenting with pulmonary nodules found to have EBV-positive diffuse large B-cell lymphoma / lymphomatoid granulomatosis. Infectious workup including cryptococcus serology was negative. Cryptococcosis was ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Cytomegalovirus and cryptococcus serology were both negative.

rationale: A 66-year-old male with refractory nodular sclerosis Hodgkin lymphoma presenting with recurrent fever and pulmonary involvement. Infectious evaluation showed negative cytomegalovirus and cryptococcus serology. Cryptococcosis was ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Tests, such as CSF VDRL, coccidioides antibodies, cryptococcus antigen, HSV PCR, oligoclonal bands, flow cytometry, and paraneoplastic autoantibody panels, were all negative or normal.

rationale: A 60-year-old female presenting with encephalopathy, aphasia, and white matter lesions diagnosed with neuronal intranuclear inclusion disease (NIID). Testing for CSF cryptococcus antigen was negative. Cryptococcosis was ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Other mycosis infections (cryptococcosis, histoplasmosis, and coccidioidomycosis) and parasitoses (trypanosomiasis) were ruled out through appropriate serological tests.

rationale: A 65-year-old female with postoperative acute intermittent porphyria crisis and primary hypoadrenalism with bilateral adrenal enlargement. Cryptococcosis was ruled out through serological testing -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Cerebrospinal fluid examination was generally normal and mycobacterium spp. and cryptococcus were not detected.

rationale: A 40-year-old male presenting with chronic headache and cranial neuropathies found to have a clival mass diagnosed as IgG4-related disease. CSF examination showed that cryptococcus was not detected. Cryptococcosis was ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: The cerebrospinal fluid examination (CSF) was performed to rule out intracranial infection, and no positive results were seen in the CSF, including CSF routine, culture, Cryptococcus neoformans, Mycobacterium tuberculosis and NGS.
evidence_items.test_name: CSF Cryptococcus neoformans culture and NGS

rationale: A 40-year-old female with Burkholderia cepacia subcutaneous abscess following encephalitis-induced brain death. Evaluation of CSF for intracranial infection showed negative results for Cryptococcus neoformans culture and NGS -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Other infectious workups including CMV, EBV, Lyme, Rocky Mountain spotted fever, Cryptococcus, and chlamydia were all negative.

rationale: A 61-year-old female post-liver transplant presenting with fever and acute liver injury diagnosed with Ehrlichia chaffeensis infection. Infectious workup including Cryptococcus was negative -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: All other virological and microbiological CSF investigations were negative (antibody indices for CMV/HSV/VZV, CMV pp65 antigen, EBV antibodies and PCR, JCV PCR, HIV antigen ELISA, tuberculosis culture and PCR, aspergillus antigen ELISA, leptospirosis antibodies, cryptococcus antigen immunodiffusion, toxoplasmosis antibodies, borrelia antibodies, culture for neisseria and brucella and an unspecific culture for other pathogenic and non-pathogenic bacteria)

rationale: A 49-year-old male with MS on natalizumab presenting with necrotizing retinitis and cerebral vasculitis diagnosed with VZV infection. CSF cryptococcus antigen immunodiffusion was negative -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: negative Cryptococcus haemolyticus capsule antigen test

rationale: A 59-year-old male presenting with paroxysmal cough, high fever, and pulmonary nodules diagnosed with Nocardia farcinica pneumonia and bacteremia. Cryptococcal capsule antigen test was negative -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Mycological and parasitological examinations were negative for cryptococcosis and toxoplasmosis, in particular in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF).

rationale: A 66-year-old male with glioblastoma on chronic dexamethasone presenting with septic shock and fatal cerebral invasive aspergillosis. CSF examination was negative for cryptococcosis -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: We also tested for Cryptococcus neoformans (agglutination test), Cytomegalovirus spp. (antigenemia), tuberculosis (three gastric lavages) and respiratory viruses (nasal secretion tests), with all negative results.

rationale: A 2-year-old male with acute lymphoblastic leukemia who developed pulmonary nodules attributable to pulmonary alveolar calcification secondary to hypercalcemia. Testing for Cryptococcus neoformans by agglutination was negative -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Ziehl-Neelsen staining for acid-fast bacilli and Cryptococcus neoformans smear test in the CSF were negative.

rationale: A 10-year-old male presenting with ataxia and mood disturbance diagnosed with anti-Homer-3 autoimmune cerebellar ataxia. CSF smear for Cryptococcus neoformans was negative -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: The patient had negative blood and sputum cultures, negative serological test for Cryptococcus and Aspergillus, negative sputum for PCP and acid-fast bacilli

rationale: A 72-year-old female presenting with respiratory failure diagnosed with organizing pneumonia and myelodysplastic syndrome. Serological test for Cryptococcus was negative -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: The search for Cryptococcus antigen was negative, as well.

rationale: A 44-year-old male with HIV and Burkitt lymphoma who developed conus medullaris and brain lesions proven on biopsy to be Toxoplasma tachyzoites. CSF search for Cryptococcus antigen was negative -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: As part of further assessment, the patient underwent screening for HIV 1/2; hepatitis A, B, C; infectious mononucleosis; Ehrlichia; Cryptococcus; and parvovirus infection, which were all negative.

rationale: A 31-year-old male presenting with aseptic meningitis symptoms and pancytopenia diagnosed with CD5-negative mantle cell lymphoma with CNS involvement. Screening for Cryptococcus was negative -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Serologic test results for blood and urine for coccidioidomycosis, cryptococcosis, toxoplasmosis, and tuberculosis were negative

rationale: A 40-year-old male with advanced HIV presenting with pulmonary cavitary lesions and cerebellar mass diagnosed with Emmonsia helica fungal infection. Serologic testing for cryptococcosis was negative and CSF fungal cultures were negative -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: No obvious abnormalities in Cryptococcus antigen detection, Mycobacterium TB identification, and for rifampicin resistance testing.

rationale: A 49-year-old male welder with pulmonary lesions diagnosed with siderosis and tuberculosis. Cryptococcus antigen testing showed no abnormalities -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: real-time PCR assay for pathogens associated with CNS infection [herpes simplex virus (HSV)1, HSV2, varicella zoster virus (VZV), human herpesvirus (HHV)6, cytomegalovirus (CMV), enterovirus, parechovirus, Neisseria meningitidis, Haemophilus influenzae, Streptococcus pneumoniae, E. coli, Listeria monocytogenes, and Cryptococcus neoformans] was negative.
evidence_items.test_name: CSF real-time PCR for Cryptococcus neoformans

rationale: A 62-year-old female presenting with foot drop, wrist drop, and central neuropathic pain diagnosed with microscopic polyangiitis (MPA). CSF real-time PCR for Cryptococcus neoformans and other CNS pathogens was negative -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Histoplasmosis antigen, acid fast bacilli (AFB), and Cryptococcus antibody tests did not yield a positive result;

rationale: A male patient with newly diagnosed HIV presenting in septic shock with multiorgan failure and ARDS, initially managed as miliary tuberculosis. Infectious workup for opportunistic pathogens was performed, and Cryptococcus antibody testing was negative. Sputum culture grew Candida albicans and autopsy definitively confirmed diffuse coccidioidomycosis. Cryptococcosis was evaluated, tested negative, and ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Subsequent CSF cultures revealed no growth of bacteria, no Borrelia antibodies, and viral/bacterial PCR (E. coli, hemophilus influenzae, Listeria monocytogenes, Neisseria meningitidis, hemolytic streptococcus, streptococcus pneumoniae, cytomegalovirus, enterovirus, herpes simplex virus, varicella zoster, Cryptococcus, and micromiome 16S/18S), and flowcytometry, and cytological analysis for malignancy were negative.

rationale: A 62-year-old female with seropositive rheumatoid arthritis presenting with headache and gait impairment. Brain MRI showed patchy meningeal enhancement and CSF analysis showed mononuclear pleocytosis. Infectious etiology workup including viral and bacterial multiplex PCR covering Cryptococcus was negative, and meningeal biopsy confirmed rheumatoid meningitis. Cryptococcosis was tested and ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: both the blood tuberculosis T cell spot test (T-SPOT. TB) and the CSF cryptococcal capsule antigen assays were negative.

rationale: A 38-year-old male presenting with fever, headache, and scattered limb rashes found to have lymphocytic pleocytosis. Infectious diagnostic evaluation for central nervous system pathogens was performed: CSF smears for Cryptococcus and CSF cryptococcal capsule antigen assays were negative. Metagenomic NGS identified HIV-1 RNA in CSF, confirming acute HIV aseptic meningitis. Cryptococcosis was tested and ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: The polymerase chain reactions (PCR) for Mycobacterium tuberculosis, Cryptococcus spp, Toxoplasma gondii, and JCV were negative, which permitted the initiation of highly active antiretroviral therapy (HAART).

rationale: A middle-aged male with newly diagnosed HIV presenting with right hemifacial hyposensitivity and left arm weakness. Brain MRI showed white matter lesions suggestive of PML. CSF examination including multiplex PCR for Cryptococcus spp was negative. Autopsy confirmed progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy with JCV-positive immunohistochemistry and PCR. Cryptococcosis was tested and ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: However, her CSF cultures were negative for histoplasma, tuberculosis, AFB, Cryptococcus, cytospin, fungus, and viruses.

rationale: A 37-year-old female presenting with headaches, vomiting, vision changes, papilledema, and sixth nerve palsy after epidural anesthesia. CSF analysis showed pleocytosis and low glucose, but CSF fungal cultures were negative for Cryptococcus. Laminectomy biopsy and culture grew Candida dubliniensis, confirming Candida intradural abscess. Cryptococcosis was evaluated, tested negative, and ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Preliminary etiological investigations excluded the presence of necrotizing autoimmune myopathy, cryptococcosis, tuberculosis, and toxoplasmosis, but Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) RNA was positive (2.55x106 copies/muL).

rationale: A 37-year-old male with AIDS presenting with headache and severe muscle pain. Diagnostic evaluation excluded cryptococcosis, tuberculosis, toxoplasmosis, and necrotizing autoimmune myopathy, while mNGS of muscle biopsy and CSF definitively identified Trachipleistophora hominis, establishing microsporidial encephalitis and myositis. Cryptococcosis was excluded -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Negative results were reported in the following CSF etiological investigations: polymerase chain reaction for tuberculosis, bacteria and fungi cultures, India Ink stain for Cryptococcus, and IgG and IgM antibodies targeting various viruses and parasites.
evidence_items.test_name: CSF India ink stain and fungal culture

rationale: A 30-year-old female presenting with progressive headache, nausea, vomiting, vision impairment, and elevated intracranial pressure (>400 mmH2O). Lumbar puncture CSF analysis revealed pleocytosis and elevated protein; CSF India ink stain for Cryptococcus as well as fungal cultures were negative. Histopathology confirmed primary diffuse leptomeningeal gliomatosis. Cryptococcosis was tested and ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: cryptococcus antigens in the blood were excluded.

rationale: An 8-year-old female presenting with severe hypereosinophilia, ischemic stroke, and myocarditis, later developing orbital cellulitis-like involvement. Extensive infectious workup was conducted to exclude secondary causes of hypereosinophilia, and cryptococcus antigens in blood were excluded. Final diagnosis was eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA). Cryptococcosis was tested and ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) gram stain, culture and a CSF PCR Panel (with targets for H.influenzae, L.monocytogenes, N.meningitidis, S.agalactiae, S.pneumoniae, Cytomegalovirus, Enterovirus, Herpes simplex virus 1 and 2, Human herpesvirus 6, Human parechovirus, Varicella Zoster virus, Cryptococcus neoformans/gatti, and E.coli K1) failed to reveal an infectious etiology.

rationale: A young female presenting with rapid neurological decline and death following an upper respiratory infection. Infectious workup including CSF gram stain, cultures, and CSF multiplex PCR panel covering Cryptococcus neoformans/gattii failed to reveal an infectious etiology. Autopsy and molecular testing diagnosed adenovirus serotype 4 associated acute disseminated encephalomyelitis (ADEM). Cryptococcosis was tested and ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: However, antibody testing for M. tuberculosis and viruses in the blood and smear tests for M. tuberculosis and Cryptococcus in CSF showed negative results.

rationale: A female patient presenting with paroxysmal dyskinesia and mild fever initially suspected of having intracranial infection due to decreased CSF glucose and mild pleocytosis. Diagnostic testing for infectious agents was performed, and smear tests for Cryptococcus and M. tuberculosis in CSF were negative. Genetic testing confirmed Glut1 deficiency syndrome (SLC2A1 mutation). Cryptococcosis was tested and ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Cryptococcus antigen testing of both CSF and serum was negative.

rationale: A male in his 40s presenting with facial pain, headache, confusion, and neck stiffness. CSF showed pleocytosis, elevated protein, and polymicrobial bacterial morphology on Gram stain, while Cryptococcus antigen testing of both CSF and serum was negative. Next-generation sequencing identified oral flora bacteria causing meningoencephalitis. Cryptococcosis was tested and ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Blood and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis was done to rule out other neurological illness such as tuberculous meningitis, toxoplasmosis, lymphoma, and cryptococcal meningitis.

rationale: A 28-year-old female with HIV presenting with headache and vomiting, found to have papilledema with anemic retinopathy. Lumbar puncture revealed opening pressure of 300 mm H2O. CSF and blood analyses were performed to rule out opportunistic neurological infections including cryptococcal meningitis, which were negative. Diagnosed with intracranial hypertension secondary to zidovudine-induced severe anemia, with complete recovery after stopping AZT and blood transfusions -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: A meningitis/encephalitis pathogen panel was negative: it tested for Escherichia coli, Haemophilus influenzae, Listeria monocytogenes, Neisseria meningitides, Streptococcus agalactiae, Streptococcus pneumoniae, cytomegalovirus, enterovirus, herpes simplex virus 1 and 2 (HSV-1 and HSV-2), human herpesvirus 6 (HHV-6), human parechovirus, varicella zoster virus (VZV), Cryptococcus neoformans, and Cryptococcus gattii.

rationale: A 31-year-old woman with sickle cell disease (HbSC), COVID-19, and influenza A who developed acute hypoxemic respiratory failure and coma due to encephalomyelitis and right internal carotid artery thrombosis. Lumbar puncture was performed; the BioFire meningitis/encephalitis panel specifically testing for Cryptococcus neoformans and Cryptococcus gattii was negative, and CSF cultures were negative -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: VDRL was positive, but the titer decreased to 1/4 of the initial values and Cryptococcus antigens were negative.

rationale: A 44-year-old renal transplant female presenting with bilateral progressive visual loss diagnosed with neurosyphilis-associated retinopathy (VDRL positive 1:2048, CSF lymphocytic pleocytosis and positive VDRL). Infectious CSF testing confirmed Cryptococcus antigens were negative. Patient recovered visual acuity on intravenous penicillin G -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Cerebrospinal fluid was negative for CMV and Cryptococcus sp.

rationale: A 35-year-old male with membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis on corticosteroids presenting with vision loss, bilateral retinal detachment, and multiple intracerebral lesions. Cerebrospinal fluid was tested and negative for Cryptococcus sp. Brain biopsy subsequently demonstrated Nocardia abscess. Cryptococcosis was ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Microbiological studies of CSF using FilmArray Meningitis/Encephalitis panel (BioFire Diagnostics, Salt Lake City, UT), which detects Escherichia coli, Haemophilus influenzae, Listeria monocytogenes, Neisseria meningitidis, Streptococcus agalactia and streptococcus pneumoniae, Cytomegalovirus, Enterovirus, Herpes simplex virus (HSV)-1, HSV-2, Human herpesvirus-6, Human parechovirus, Varicella zoster virus, and Cryptococcus, were all negative.

rationale: A 60-year-old female presenting with acute visual loss and optic neuritis after COVID-19 vaccination. Microbiological evaluation of CSF using the FilmArray Meningitis/Encephalitis panel covering Cryptococcus was negative. Patient was diagnosed with anti-MOG optic neuritis and responded completely to corticosteroids -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: G test, GM test, blood cultures, and Cryptococcus capsular antigen tests were performed several times during the course of each patient's disease, and all tests were negative.

rationale: A 17-year-old female presenting with acute liver failure after Chinese patent medicine and subsequent pulmonary infiltrates. Extensive infectious workup was conducted; Cryptococcus capsular antigen tests were performed repeatedly and were negative -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Aspergillus, Candida mannan, and Cryptococcus neoformans antigens were negative.

rationale: A 46-year-old male presenting with fever, fatigue, bacterial peritonitis, and fungal pneumonia. Blood testing confirmed Cryptococcus neoformans antigen was negative. Autopsy subsequently revealed invasive fungal pneumonia with angioinvasive hyphae -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: The Cryptococcus neoformans capsular antigen and tubercle Bacillus tests in both CSF and blood were negative.
evidence_items.test_name: CSF and serum Cryptococcus neoformans capsular antigen test

rationale: A 61-year-old female presenting with fever, chills, lung cavities, and cerebral lesions caused by disseminated Nocardia farcinica. Testing for Cryptococcus neoformans capsular antigen in both CSF and blood was negative -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Serum beta-D-glucan, galactomannan antigen, Histoplasma antigen, and Cryptococcus antigens were also negative.

rationale: A 65-year-old female presenting with fever, severe neutropenia, lung nodules, and an anterior mediastinal mass diagnosed as thymoma. Evaluation for invasive fungal infection was negative, specifically including serum Cryptococcus antigens -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: His CSF was negative for herpes simplex viruses 1 and 2, Adenovirus, Enterovirus, Cryptococcus, and Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

rationale: A 27-year-old male with ulcerative colitis presenting with acute headache and left eye proptosis. Infectious workup of CSF specifically tested negative for Cryptococcus. Brain biopsy revealed necrotizing vasculitis confirming PR3-ANCA mediated cerebral and orbital vasculitis -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: CSF study showed elevated total protein, but no evidence of cryptococcal infection or bacterial meningoencephalitis.

rationale: A 72-year-old male with a remote history of systemic cryptococcosis presenting with acute cognitive decline, apraxia, and FLAIR hyperintensities. Recurrent CNS cryptococcosis was suspected; empiric amphotericin B was initiated without improvement. CSF studies showed no evidence of cryptococcal infection, and the patient showed rapid clinical and radiological recovery on high-dose corticosteroids, confirming cerebral amyloid angiopathy-related inflammation (CAA-ri) -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Multiplex-PCR (Filmarray, BioFire, Biomerieux Lyon, France) from CSF was negative for cytomegalovirus (CMV), enterovirus, herpes simplex viruses 1 and 2, human herpesvirus 6, human parechovirus, varicella zoster virus, Cryptococcus neoformans and gattii, E. coli K1, Haemophilus influenzae, Listeria monocytogenes, Neisseria meningitides as well as Streptococcus agalactiae and pneumoniae.

rationale: A 2-year-old boy presenting with acute unilateral left sixth nerve palsy following a recent respiratory infection / COVID-19 exposure. CSF multiplex PCR (BioFire FilmArray) testing was negative for all viral and bacterial targets, as well as Cryptococcus neoformans and gattii. Diagnosed with post-COVID-19 benign abducens nerve palsy. Cryptococcosis ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Cryptococcus latex agglutination test was negative.

rationale: A 45-year-old female greening worker presenting with dyspnea, left bronchial artery-pulmonary artery shunt, and pulmonary nodules. Bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) cryptococcus latex agglutination test was negative, and BALF bacterial/fungal cultures were negative. Cryptococcosis tested and ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: The CSF smear stained with India ink showed no cryptococcus. The test result for cryptococcal capsular antigen in the CSF was negative. Initial CSF culture yielded no pathogens.
evidence_items.test_name: CSF India ink, CrAg, and fungal culture

rationale: A 39-year-old man presenting with acute speech disorder and right hemiplegia initially suspected as acute cerebral infarction. Diagnostic lumbar puncture demonstrated that CSF smear stained with India ink was negative for cryptococcus, CSF cryptococcal capsular antigen was negative, and CSF culture yielded no pathogens. Cryptococcosis ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Blood and sputum cultures, autoimmune serologic tests, and serologic tests for Coccidioides and Cryptococcus were negative.

rationale: A 25-year-old HIV-positive male with pulmonary Kaposi sarcoma presenting with progressive dyspnea and expectoration of bronchial casts. Workup for infectious causes including serologic tests for Coccidioides and Cryptococcus were negative. Histopathology confirmed plastic bronchitis secondary to KS -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: CSF tuberculosis polymerase chain reaction (PCR), coccidioides antibody, and cryptococcus antigen were all negative.

rationale: A 64-year-old female with metastatic gastric adenocarcinoma presenting with headache, dizziness, hearing loss, and elevated CSF opening pressure (>55 cm H2O). CSF infectious workup including tuberculosis PCR, coccidioides antibody, and cryptococcus antigen were all negative. CSF cytology and MRI confirmed leptomeningeal carcinomatosis -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Extensive testing for infectious encephalitis was unremarkable (CSF PCR for E. coli K1, H. influenzae, L. monocytogenes, N. meningitidis, S. agalactiae, S. pneumoniae, Cytomegalovirus, Enterovirus, Herpes simplex 1 and 2, Herpes 6, Parechovirus, Varicella zoster, and Cryptococcus neoformans).
